summary: Joined as founding engineer. Owned backend, infrastructure, and ingestion from day zero: hybrid vector + graph retrieval under 200ms, 100k+ files indexed daily, full self-hosted Kubernetes stack. Promoted to Product Lead. Helped ship the platform that raised a $6.5M seed. Now leading product while building a graph database from scratch on object storage, targeting ~10x multi-hop performance vs Neo4j on our workloads.

responsibilities: Promoted to Product Lead after owning backend and infrastructure from day zero on the team that raised a $6.5M seed.
Lead product for HydraDB's context graph platform: roadmap, prioritization, and how customers put company knowledge into agents that actually work in production.
Scaled the connectors product across 30+ SaaS tools (email, tickets, CRM, warehouses including BigQuery table rows) so teams search one brain instead of twenty apps.
Grew hybrid search into a product customers trust: sub-200ms retrieval, npm + PyPI SDKs from OpenAPI, and quality that holds up past the demo.

Building a graph database from scratch on object storage: OpenCypher and Bolt for Neo4j-driver compatibility, sparse indexes, and cloud-native durability. On our multi-hop agent workloads we are seeing roughly 10x faster traversals than Neo4j.
Sole owner of the backend and infrastructure from day zero. Built and shipped indexing for 100,000+ files daily across customer orgs, at roughly 1M+ tokens per minute on average.

Self-hosted the full production stack on Kubernetes/EKS: Milvus (vector), FalkorDB (graph), ClickHouse (analytics), Kafka, Temporal, plus Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager with multi-tenant isolation.
Brought end-to-end hybrid search under 200ms, with sub-10ms queries on both Milvus and FalkorDB for real-time vector + graph retrieval.

Redesigned the full document ingestion pipeline after production pain: Temporal durable workflows, transactional inbox for exactly-once delivery, per-org Kafka topics for fair multi-tenant scheduling, claim-check for large payloads, and replay-safe multi-store sinks (vector + graph + metadata).
Migrated Kafka off a managed path that was silently losing data (MSK Serverless → Strimzi KRaft); auto-published client SDKs from OpenAPI; led the platform move from usecortex.ai to hydradb.com.

Worked as a product engineer throughout and helped shape the core offering that raised a $6.5M seed round. Now deep in the next storage layer: a graph database built from scratch (not a Neo4j wrapper) for multi-tenant company memory and ~10x multi-hop speed on our benchmarks.
Joined as a founding engineer and owned core retrieval: Pro-Search, a production RAG system with multi-step retrieval and planning.
Built scalable ingestion to process, embed, and index thousands of documents with multi-threading, async processing, and auto-scaling. Cut p50/p90 search latency by over 50%.
Increased search accuracy by about 20% through better chunking and retrieval. Shipped typed APIs and SDKs for ingestion and search.
This work became the foundation of Cortex / HydraDB as the product evolved into an ontology-first context graph platform.

Co-authored and published an IEEE paper (Big Data) on privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning. Proposed a decentralized framework combining federated learning, blockchain, and secure multi-party computation to fine-tune LLaMA 3.1 and Mistral Nemo without exposing raw training data.

Benchmarked federated versus traditional fine-tuning across 52 models and 4 datasets. Showed that federated learning achieves lower or similar variance and more stable training for sensitive domains like healthcare.
Used QLoRA (4-bit quantization) to make LLM fine-tuning feasible on resource-constrained client hardware.

Reduced response time of a Kubernetes fleet monitoring service from 8 minutes to under 1 minute (8x faster) with connection pooling, request batching, multithreading, and Redis caching across 1,000+ pods.
Built a dynamic query engine with 27 filters and 100+ sub-filters, giving DevOps teams fine-grained, real-time observability into their infrastructure.
Selected as a paid open-source mentee for LitmusChaos, a CNCF project for chaos engineering on Kubernetes.
Merged 7 PRs covering test infrastructure, interface refactoring, and code deduplication in the chaos engineering core. Drove test coverage above 90%.
Contributed to GraphQL-to-REST migration work and production-grade Go services used by the chaos platform.
